title: Every Sky Primitive an Agent uses is tracked by a Hub Document that encodes instance state as document location
content:
Each Primitive that Pattern uses opens with a **Primitive Hub Document** that "organize[s] all base information relevant to Pattern's usage" of it, and every Hub Document has the same five slots: Global Activation Status, Active Instances Directory, Completed Instances Directory, In Progress Invocations Directory, and Hub Data Repository (e.g. A.6.1.1.6.2.1.1.1, A.6.1.1.6.2.2.1.1).

The operative mechanism is that these directories are not merely indexes — they *are* the state machine. A.6.1.1.6.2.2.1.1.4 spells out the transitions: "Invocations that are completed successfully are moved to [the] Active Instances Directory, whereas failed Invocations are Archived in [the] Hub Data Repository." A.6.1.1.6.2.2.1.4 repeats it from the other side: "Once an Invocation is successfully completed, its subtree will be moved to [Active Instances]." Suspended instances get their own archive location (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.1.1.5.1.2).

Representing status as *position in a document tree* rather than as a status field has a real consequence: the state of an instance is always visible in the Atlas's own navigation, and changing state requires an Artifact edit — the same governance-gated act as any other change to the document. There is no way to silently flip an instance from failed to active, because the move is a diff.

The trade-off is redundancy: the same instance is referenced from a directory, from its own configuration document, and from a location pointer, so the structure must be kept internally consistent by hand across several sections.
description: Active, Completed and In Progress Invocations Directories plus an archive under the Hub Data Repository; a state transition is performed by moving the instance's document subtree between them.
